facts.fact: The environment of space is lethal without appropriate protection: the greatest threat in the vacuum of space derives from the lack of oxygen and pressure, although temperature and radiation also pose risks.

If the body does not get enough oxygen, then the astronaut is at risk of becoming unconscious and dying from hypoxia. In the vacuum of space, gas exchange in the lungs continues but results in the removal of all gases, including oxygen, from the bloodstream. After 9 to 12 seconds, the deoxygenated blood reaches the brain, and it results in the loss of consciousness.
Jim LeBlanc's suit pressure dropped from 3.8 psi to 0.1 psi in less than 10 seconds. He remained conscious for about 14 seconds before losing consciousness due to hypoxia.

Ebullism results from the formation of bubbles in body fluids due to reduced ambient pressure. Exposure to vacuum for up to 30 seconds is unlikely to cause permanent physical damage. Animal experiments show that rapid and complete recovery is normal for exposures shorter than 90 seconds, while longer full-body exposures are fatal.
The three crew-members of the Soyuz 11 spacecraft died of exposure to vacuum in space during a rapid depressurisation event.

sentences.text: What happens if you remove your helmet in space?
Your body swells as bodily fluids begin to boil due to the vacuum.
You lose consciousness in about 14 seconds due to lack of oxygen.
Without recompression within 90 seconds, death is unavoidable.
Removing your helmet causes rapid decompression, oxygen loss, and boiling bodily fluids, leading to unconsciousness and death within minutes.
Three astronauts died when their Soyuz capsule depressurized in 1971.

title: What Happens If You Remove Your Helmet In Space?
